note: How I enter a trade once the macro work has picked the pair and the direction. Four confluences, one pattern, one order type: a limit order placed into liquidity, never into a zone.

source.title: Once you master this strategy, trading becomes EASY
source.example: AUDCHF daily, bullish and bearish legs

pattern.intro: Every setup is the same five moves. The fake out and the liquidation are what trap the traders who bought the breakout or the retest; the continuation is the trade.
steps: Impulse breaks structure (a new high in an uptrend).
Price comes back towards the broken level.
A bounce at the breakout area. Traders go long on the retest, stops under the low they think is strong.
Price sweeps the low that broke the high and stops those traders out. Some flip short here.
The real move in the trend's direction. Both the stopped longs and the new shorts are fuel.

confluences.name: Market structure
confluences.check: Trend is clear on the daily, and the impulse is drawn from a strong low to the high that broke structure.
detail: Read momentum first: is price making higher highs (bullish) or lower lows (bearish)?
Draw the impulse: from the swing low to the high that broke structure.
The swing low only counts as a strong low if it swept liquidity to its left before the push. A low that took nothing out is weak and will likely be taken.
Stops go beyond the strong low. Nowhere else.

confluences.name: Liquidity
confluences.check: A liquidity low inside the impulse, ideally on the daily, has been marked as the entry.
detail: Liquidity lives inside the impulse only: the small pullbacks within the leg that broke structure.
Spot them on the daily as bearish candles sitting on top of a bullish leg. On a lower timeframe those are pullback lows, with demand and stop losses just underneath.
Never trade from the demand zone itself. Most demand zones get swept, which is where everyone's stop sits. Enter where the stops are, not where the buyers are.
Daily liquidity is stronger than 4H, 1H or 15m. Drop to 4H only to see the pullback lows more clearly.

confluences.name: Premium and discount
confluences.check: The entry sits at or below the 0.5 of the impulse (longs), at or above it (shorts).
detail: Fibonacci at 0, 0.5 and 1 only, anchored on the strong low and the impulse high.
A healthy pullback reaches about 0.5. Below it is discount: where longs belong.
If the fib is anchored on a weak low, the whole read is wrong. Anchor on the strong low.

confluences.name: Order flow or an open
confluences.check: The liquidity low lines up with order flow, or with a monthly, quarterly or six-monthly open.
detail: Either a fractal structure break or an order-flow area confirms the level.
Or the opens indicator (daily, weekly, monthly opens by SBTNC on TradingView).
A liquidity low that sits on a monthly, quarterly or six-monthly open is the best case: the video calls it a golden opportunity.

entry: Buy limit just under the liquidity low (sell limit just above the liquidity high). Price has to sweep the level to fill you.
Enter at the first liquidity low, stop under the second liquidity low. Tighter stop, more fills missed.
Enter at the second (deeper) liquidity low, stop under the strong low. Wider stop, safer.
Beyond a strong low: one that swept liquidity before the impulse. Never under a plain demand zone.
A new higher high (lower low for shorts). The trend runs until price takes out the lowest point of the structure.
Daily for the map and the levels. 4H to see the pullback lows. No lower-timeframe trigger: the limit order is the entry.
ltfRead: On the 4H, a clean push, pullback, push, pullback with no liquidation means the lows are still sitting there: expect them to be taken before the real push. Once price has swept the pullback low, it is ready to continue.
missing: Risk per trade and minimum reward to risk: not given. My AAA rule: 0.5 to 1% per trade, 1:3 minimum.
How long a limit order stays open, and when to cancel it if price runs without filling.

checklist: Daily trend clear and on the side of my Scorecard pair
Impulse drawn from a strong low that swept liquidity first
Liquidity low marked inside the impulse (daily, or seen on 4H)
Entry at or past 0.5 of the impulse (discount for longs, premium for shorts)
Order flow, or a monthly / quarterly / six-monthly open, at the same level
Limit just past the liquidity, stop past the strong low
Target the next higher high / lower low, at least 1:3
